slides.title: A Physics-Consistent Benchmark for Contact-Rich Human-Robot Interaction in Assistive Care
slides.highlight: This work introduces a benchmark for contact-rich human-robot interaction in assistive care, emphasizing the need for physics-aware screening beyond simple task success. It is relevant to RwB's focus on embodied social robots and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: A physics-consistent benchmark for assistive care showing that task completion does not imply physically valid contact.
card.key_idea: Combines a deformable, passively responding human model calibrated against real manikin force-indentation measurements with a leak-free, vision-only observation protocol and physics-aware scoring.
card.evaluation: Evaluated State Machine, VoxPoser, and $\pi_{0.5}$ across 7 bathing tasks (140 runs/method) using task success, peak force, and joint-limit margins.
card.limitation: Uses a medical manikin instead of human tissue and reuses forearm calibration for the upper arm.

slides.title: A Wearable Pneumatic Device for Continuous, Closed-Loop, Bidirectional Tactile Interaction
slides.highlight: This research introduces a wearable pneumatic system that unifies tactile sensing and haptic feedback to enable real-time bidirectional touch interaction. It demonstrates improved teleoperated manipulation by reducing applied pressures and task duration while lowering mental workload.

card.one_liner: A wearable pneumatic device enabling bidirectional tactile interaction by using the same modality for sensing and feedback.
card.key_idea: A distributed architecture using proportional piezoelectric valves and local closed-loop control to regulate textile pneumatic pouches as both sensors and actuators for real-time haptic mirroring.
card.evaluation: Tested via device characterization (34.2Hz bandwidth) and human studies (n=25). Results showed improved teleoperation: 23.1% lower applied pressure and 18.1% lower mental demand.
card.limitation: Weight discrimination accuracy dropped significantly in complex 3-element teleoperated tasks; some users conflated robotic system latency with haptic device latency.

slides.title: N0-Foundation: Towards the Age of Tactile Intelligence
slides.highlight: This work introduces a visuo-tactile representation model and a large-scale dataset to improve physical contact state perception, supporting HyECHO's goal of multimodal social perception in hybrid teams.

card.one_liner: A comprehensive tactile-centric foundation for embodied manipulation integrating hardware, large-scale data, and unified representations.
card.key_idea: NeoForce learns hardware-agnostic tactile representations by using dense three-axis force fields as unified supervision across diverse visuo-tactile sensor designs.
card.evaluation: Evaluated via NeoReal (real-world) and NeoSim (simulated) suites; results show policies benefit from physical contact states over device-specific signals.

slides.title: Facet-0: A Robotic Foundation Model for Contact-Rich Precise Manipulation
slides.tldr: FOUNDATION MODEL FOR SUB-MILLIMETER CONTACT-RICH ASSEMBLY
slides.highlight: Facet-0 utilizes a joint action-wrench proposal and a distributional Action-Wrench Critic to manage contact consequences, aligning with MOSAIC's focus on physics and force-based skill acquisition for precise assembly.

card.one_liner: Facet-0 is a robotic foundation model for sub-millimeter assembly that predicts and values contact consequences.
card.key_idea: It uses flow-matching to jointly generate action chunks and predicted wrist-wrenches, refined by a distributional Action-Wrench Critic and a lightweight bounded actor for local adaptation.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on five computer-assembly tasks using ManuFacet-1K; achieved 82% mean success vs 15% for the strongest baseline with 0.5mm accuracy.
card.limitation: The hardest task (LEVER), containing only contact-critical presses without free-space steps, only reached 50% success.

slides.title: SpectraTac: A Compact Camera-Free Optical Tactile Sensor with Distributed Color Sensing
slides.highlight: SpectraTac introduces a low-cost, compact tactile sensor that uses distributed color sensing instead of cameras to estimate 3D force and contact regions.

card.one_liner: SpectraTac is a compact, camera-free optical tactile sensor using distributed color sensing for 3D force estimation.
card.key_idea: Combines RGB illumination with three distributed RGBC sensors in a PDMS layer; a ResMLP decodes low-dimensional spatio-spectral features into force and contact-region data.
card.evaluation: Evaluated using a 6-axis F/T sensor; achieved 99.9% contact-region accuracy and 3D force MAEs between 0.161N and 0.429N. Results appear trustworthy.
card.limitation: Future work is needed to improve spatial resolution, force decoupling, dynamic perception, and long-term robustness.

slides.title: DeicticVLA: Unifying Instruction Modes Based on Language and Deictic Gestures in a Single VLA
slides.tldr: UNIFIED VLA FOR LANGUAGE AND DEICTIC GESTURES
slides.highlight: DeicticVLA integrates language, vision-language, and visual instructions into a single model to improve target specification in manipulation tasks. It demonstrates superior performance over language-only instructions, particularly with unseen categories and novel objects.

card.one_liner: DeicticVLA unifies language, vision-language, and visual-only instructions into a single VLA for robot manipulation.
card.key_idea: Canonicalizes three instruction modes into text prompts and deictic masks, comparing RGB visual prompting and separate-channel mask prompting using a two-stage training strategy.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on LIBERO simulation and three real-world tasks. Results show VLI and VI outperform LI, especially for unseen objects and layouts.

slides.title: Anomaly Detection on Small Industrial Components via Vision-Based Tactile Sensing
slides.tldr: TACTILE ANOMALY DETECTION FOR INDUSTRIAL COMPONENTS
slides.highlight: This work evaluates unsupervised anomaly detection using vision-based tactile sensors to capture fine surface geometry. It is relevant to HyECHO's focus on multimodal perception by demonstrating how tactile data can complement optical sensing for detailed state observation.

card.one_liner: Systematic evaluation of unsupervised anomaly detection using vision-based tactile sensing for small industrial components.
card.key_idea: Benchmarked four feature-embedding methods (SPADE, PaDiM, FAPM, InReaCh) using a GelSight Mini sensor, focusing on nominal sample size, cross-position generalization, and image resolution.
card.evaluation: Tested on five real industrial components using AUROC, AUPRC, and AUC-PRO@0.01. Results show SPADE leads in LR localization, while FAPM excels in HR.
card.limitation: Soft-interface gel wear limits the number of possible contacts, and the dataset is not publicly released due to confidentiality.

slides.title: CometVLA: Co-Training on an Embodied Data Pyramid towards Physical Understanding
slides.tldr: ENHANCING VLA MODELS WITH EMBODIED PHYSICAL UNDERSTANDING
slides.highlight: This work introduces CometVLA and a corresponding benchmark to improve physical commonsense in manipulation tasks, supporting RwB's focus on embodied AI and human-robot interaction.

card.one_liner: CometVLA improves robot manipulation by co-training a VLA model on an embodied physical VQA pyramid.
card.key_idea: Uses CometData (embodied VQA) and Global Action Prior (GAP) tokens as a bottleneck to integrate physical commonsense into a diffusion-based action expert without corrupting the VLM backbone.
card.evaluation: Evaluated on RoboTwin simulation and real-world G1 robot tasks; outperformed baselines like π0.5 and showed positive correlation between CometBench VQA and success rates.
card.limitation: Correlation analysis used a narrow range of success rates (~85%), and real-robot testing covered only a limited subset of manipulation behaviors.
